section1.title: What is a couple check-up?
section1.p1: A couple check-up is a questionnaire that both partners fill in separately, so they can compare their answers afterwards. It doesn't measure personality compatibility: it looks at whether you want the same life. For example: "Having children: yes, definitely, yes, probably, I don't know yet, or no". If one of you answers "yes, definitely" and the other "no", that's a gap, and it's the kind of gap you'd better know about early!
section1.p2: Couples counsellors have used this kind of questionnaire for a long time, especially before a wedding. This one is done without a counsellor, on your phone, and takes 20 to 25 minutes each. It asks very concrete questions: a joint account or not, whose family at Christmas, city or countryside, phones at the table, or what each of you calls cheating.
section1.p3: At the end, you see where you agree, where your answers are close, and where they drift apart. The point isn't to get a score, it's to know what to talk about, and in what order.

section2.title: The twelve areas of the check-up
section2.p1: The questions are grouped into twelve areas, from the simplest to the most intimate. You start with everyday life to warm up, and finish with how each of you is experiencing the relationship right now.
points: Everyday life at home: chores, what each of you keeps track of, tidiness, the rhythm of evenings and weekends.
Time together and time for yourself: how much time together, the need to be alone, going out, holidays.
Family and friends: the in-laws, the end-of-year holidays, nights out without the other.
Work and ambitions: the place of work, a career change, a pay gap.
Money: joint account or not, splitting costs, saving, big purchases.
Where and how to live: moving in, city or countryside, buying a home, moving for the other's job.
Children: wanting them or not, when, how many, how to raise them.
Values: religion, marriage, what matters most to each of you.
Communication and arguments: saying what bothers you, arguing, making up.
Trust and fidelity: phones, exes, jealousy, what counts as cheating.
Intimacy and tenderness: desire, tenderness, and how you talk about them.
How you're doing: eight questions about how each of you feels in the relationship today.
section2.p2: No area can be removed, and that's on purpose: if one of you doesn't want children and the other does, that's exactly what the check-up should show. The questions do adapt to your situation, though. A couple who don't live together yet get "living together, when?" instead of "who does the chores?", and a couple who already have children get "another child?" instead of "do you want them?".

section3.title: How it works
section3.p1: Here's how the check-up works, from start to finish:
points: You create the check-up: your two first names, and seven questions about your situation (do you live together, do you have children, etc.).
You invite your partner: you send them a link, by message or with a QR code.
Each of you answers separately: about 90 questions, in one go or in several. Every answer is saved straight away, and each of you can see how far the other has got, without ever seeing their answers.
You discover your result: as soon as you've both finished, for free.
If you want it, the full report: all your gaps, both your answers and what you need to talk about them, for {{prix}}.
section3.p2: On the big questions (children, where to live, marriage, what counts as cheating...), you can mark an answer "non-negotiable". If your answers clash on a point one of you marked that way, the report shows it first: it's a sticking point.

section4.title: Why each of you answers separately
section4.p1: When you answer together on the same screen, you watch the other's reaction before choosing, and you often end up giving the answer that pleases. On your own, you answer for yourself. In fact, many couples discover gaps on topics they thought they'd already talked about.
section4.p2: That's also why questions about sharing the chores are answered with "mostly me", "both of us equally" or "mostly the other". When each of you thinks they do more, the check-up shows it in black and white, and it's often the starting point for a much calmer conversation than usual. To go further on that particular topic, there's also our test on what weighs on each of your minds.
section4.p3: If you're looking for a quick test to do together on the same phone instead, your love compatibility can be measured in five minutes. The check-up takes longer because it goes into the detail of your life.

section5.title: What's free, and what you pay for
section5.p1: Answering is free, for both of you. When you've finished, your overall result is free too: your agreement percentage, your relationship forecast, a bar for each area, the number of your gaps and sticking points, and one of your gaps in full, with both your answers and the guide to talking about it.
section5.p2: The full report costs {{prix}} for both of you, paid once, by either of you. It contains all your gaps with both your answers, why each topic matters, two questions to talk about it and what's best not to say, your next four conversations in order, what brings you together, and the forecast question by question. You can print it or keep it as a PDF.
section5.tip: The price is the same for everyone, there's no subscription, and you get your money back within {{jours}} days if you're not satisfied.

section6.title: Your answers stay between you
section6.p1: There's no account and no email address to give. Each of you gets into the check-up with your own link, which contains a secret key we don't store in plain text. Nobody but the two of you sees your answers, and your partner only sees them once you've both finished.
section6.p2: An unpaid check-up is erased 60 days after the last answer, a paid one six months after payment. Either of you can also delete it at any time, in one click, from the report. The details are in our privacy policy.
section6.tip: This check-up shows each of you the other's answers. If you're afraid of your partner, it isn't made for your situation: in the UK, the National Domestic Abuse Helpline (0808 2000 247) answers for free, 24/7, and in the US the National Domestic Violence Hotline (1-800-799-7233).

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How long does the check-up take?
faq.a1: Allow 20 to 25 minutes each, for about 90 questions. You don't have to do it all at once: every answer is saved, and you pick up where you left off, on the same phone or with your personal link.
faq.q2: Will my partner see all my answers?
faq.a2: Yes, once you've both finished: the report puts your two answers side by side, that's the whole point of the check-up. While you're answering, though, nobody sees anything, and each of you only sees how far the other has got.
faq.q3: Can we do the check-up if we don't live together or don't have children?
faq.a3: Yes. At the start, you describe your situation in seven questions, and the questions adapt: a couple who don't live together get "living together, when?", a couple without children get "do you want them?", etc. No area is removed, though, because your wishes matter as much as your current situation.
faq.q4: What if we find out we disagree on lots of things?
faq.a4: It happens a lot, and it isn't bad news: a gap you know about can be discussed, a gap you don't know about ends up blowing up at the wrong moment. The report helps you choose where to start, with questions to talk about it calmly.
faq.q5: Does the check-up replace couples therapy?
faq.a5: No. It's a tool to put words to what you're going through and know what to talk about. If you're going through a difficult time, a couples counsellor can help you go further, and the report can even be a starting point with them.
faq.a6: By card, Apple Pay or Google Pay, on Stripe's secure payment page. A single payment of {{prix}}, by either of you, unlocks the report for both of you. You get a receipt by email, and you get your money back within {{jours}} days if you're not satisfied.
faq.q7: Can we do the check-up again later?
faq.a7: Yes, and it's actually a good idea: doing it again in a year shows what has changed between you. Each check-up is separate, you just create a new one.
faq.a8: They're only used for your check-up. They're erased 60 days after the last answer if the check-up isn't paid for, six months after payment if it is, and either of you can delete them straight away from the report.
